wy_2_sex_god_wall.blurb: A short wall of lower-angle sport climbing on the right side of Fairfield East, up Sinks Canyon near Lander. The twelve routes here are mostly 5.10, with a few easier lines down in the 5.6 to 5.9 range, so it suits climbers stepping up from moderates as well as those warming up. Climbs are brief, on pockets and crimps, and the stone is clean and pleasant. It is the first wall you meet when the approach trail reaches the base of the cliff, which makes it a quick, convenient stop for an easy session.

wy_mount_moran.blurb: Mount Moran is a massive peak at the north end of the Teton Range, rising high above Jackson Lake in Grand Teton National Park. Most of the dozen routes here are long alpine and trad lines, running from moderate fifth class up to the low 5.12s, with a few in the 5.9 to 5.10 range. It sees far fewer climbers than the Grand because getting to the base is a real undertaking: most parties paddle String and Leigh Lakes, then route-find on foot. Plan on a multi-day trip even when the technical climbing is short.

wy_4_the_hideout.blurb: The Hideout is a small sport sector at Fossil Hill near Lander, a few minutes along the cliff band from the main wall. It holds about twelve routes, mostly 5.11 and low 5.12, with one or two easier lines at 5.8 and 5.9. Trees give belayers more shade than the main wall offers, so it is a handy fallback when that wall is crowded, windy or hot. The climbing is steep and powerful, with deep pockets and big jugs, and feels closer to Wild Iris than to the rest of the hill.

wy_ambush_peak.blurb: Ambush Peak is a jagged granite summit above the East Fork Valley in the Wind River Range. The twelve routes are all alpine, many of them long multi-pitch lines, with grades mostly between 5.9 and 5.10 and a few at the easy and hard ends. The east face is steep and intimidating, with slabs below and corners and roofs above, while the back side is a simple walk-off. Expect adventurous climbing with old pitons and sparse fixed anchors, and very few other parties. The approach is a long backcountry hike in.

wy_black_magic.blurb: Black Magic is a single 12 to 15 foot boulder in Brown's Park, Fremont Canyon, with a dozen problems. One side is steeply overhung and the other shorter and vertical. Grades run from V3 up to V11, though the middle of the range, V4 to V7, holds most of them, so there is plenty for solid boulderers and only a couple of moderates. Landings are decent with one or two pads and a spotter. It is a short walk of about five to ten minutes from the parking lot, and the area is quiet.

wy_garnet_canyon_meadows.blurb: Garnet Canyon Meadows sits where the two forks of Garnet Canyon meet in Grand Teton National Park, on the way to the Grand Teton normal routes. Avalanches have left a flat spread of boulders and willows, with crags that are cleaner than is usual in the Tetons. The twelve climbs mix alpine, trad, a little aid and boulder problems, from easy fifth class to hard 5.12 and 5.14, and boulders from V3 to V13. It is about a five-mile hike from the valley, so most people come as part of a longer trip into the canyon.

wy_ice_plant_the.blurb: The Ice Plant is a sport crag tucked into a small side canyon in Ten Sleep Canyon. It stays shady most of the day, with only brief direct sun, and mornings are best, so it is a good pick for hot days. Twelve routes run from 5.9 to 5.12, with half of them at 5.10 and a handful of 5.11s and 5.12s. One route is two pitches. The walk from the road takes roughly ten to thirty minutes, passing Wall of Denial and Raven Wall before reaching the crag on your right.

wy_john_henry_grotto.blurb: John Henry Grotto is the far-left section of Downtown in Ten Sleep Canyon, just left of the free-standing pillar called the Cigar. It is an alcove of steep sport routes aimed at strong climbers: the twelve lines here start around 5.11 and go through 5.12 into 5.13, with half in the 5.13 range. Downtown gets sun in the morning and shade later in the day. The trail starts at the right end of the large parking lot and takes about fifteen minutes, bearing left at the split.
